authorization: Bearer token issued by another tool's local runtime; user-authorized flow required
origin: field list documented; every value invented and every personally identifying value replaced by the literal sentinel <redacted-at-capture>
notes: SHAPE ONLY, and the one documented source of personally identifying data in this corpus. userId is the candidate provider_scope_id, so it is an invented opaque string rather than a redaction: a scope identity has to be stable to be useful. userLevel and userLevelName are the plan identity, and requirements forbid guessing a plan from quota size, so this endpoint matters - but userLevelName is a display name and is redacted here to show that the capture path must redact it before it reaches the database, a log or this repository. The documented optional fields avatar, bio, username, createdTime, lastLoginTime and globalId are OMITTED entirely rather than redacted, because an omitted field cannot leak. email and phone are present only as the sentinel so the redaction rule is testable; the status enum vocabulary is not published, so 'active' is illustrative and not authoritative. region matters because plan lineups and currency differ by region: the documented plan set and CNY prices are China-scoped. NOTHING from this endpoint may be persisted beyond the opaque scope identity and the plan label the user is shown, and no value from it may be logged. Every JSON response from this server is wrapped in {code, msg, data, request_id} and the HTTP status is almost always 200, so the business result is code (0 = success) and must be checked before data. Some error envelopes carry non-empty data, which is why checking the status line or the presence of data first is wrong. request_id is an invented 26-character ULID-shaped string. The server binds plain HTTP on loopback (127.0.0.1:58627 by default) and requires a bearer token for every /api/* path except the liveness probe; that token belongs to another tool's runtime and must never be captured, stored or committed. The whole API is documented as experimental: endpoints, fields and event types may change in any version, so the /openapi.json served by the version actually in use has to be re-validated at runtime before any of these shapes is trusted.
